$comment: Shared input/expected vectors for VfTooltip. The TypeScript rules in tooltip/state.ts run every section; the PHP mirror in packages/razor/src/Support/TooltipState.php runs the sections a server can decide (listed in $serverRules) and deliberately has no method for the others - the classes, the arrow offset and the description relationship are decided in the browser once the tooltip opens, and a server never renders one open. The contract of the reference at fd793696, quirks included: the flip pair is top/bottom for every placement; --top and --bottom follow the computed placement on the tooltip and on the arrow, and neither is written for any other side; the arrow offset is 0 on an axis missing either number; teleportTo false or null renders in place and anything that is not a string means body; content is JavaScript truthiness of the text or the presence of a slot, so an empty text is none and a whitespace-only text or "0" is some; aria-describedby follows the open state alone, content or not. `null` in `teleportTo` or `text` is JSON null; an absent key is `undefined`.

resolveTooltipContentClasses.$why: The computed placement decides the modifier by its prefix.
Any other side gets neither modifier: two conditions, not a two-way choice.

resolveTooltipArrowClasses.$why: Unlike VfPopover's arrow, which is --bottom for everything that is not on top.

resolveTooltipArrowOffset.$why: A missing base zeroes that axis only.

resolveTooltipTeleport.$why: Explicit null renders in place in Vue. Razor reads a null attribute as not given (its adapter convention) and spells this `false`, so the PHP mirror skips this one vector.
true is not a string and not an element: body, not in place.
disableTeleport wins over a selector, which is still resolved.

resolveTooltipHasContent.$why: No text and no slot: an open tooltip renders nothing and its reference dangles.
"0" is a non-empty string, truthy in JavaScript - not falsy as in PHP.
A slot renders whatever the text is.
